audit_findings.title: Gross June 2026 cash may include an unpaid declared dividend
audit_findings.magnitude: $20.9 million cash payment, computed as $0.086 per 243.58783 million valuation shares
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds June 30 cash before deducting the cash portion of the dividend declared May 1 and paid July 21, 2026.
audit_findings.evidence: Dividends payable includes dividends declared but not yet paid and prior dividends on unvested shares of Class A common stock payable upon future vesting.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated bridge error: the 10-Q reports $24.310 million of dividends payable and specifies that $20.9 million was payable in cash, with $3.4 million settled through dividend equivalents. Deducting $20.9 million lowers scenario values by about $0.09 per share, from $2.76-$3.39 to approximately $2.67-$3.30. That is roughly 2.5%-3.1% of reported scenario equity value and does not alter the conclusion relative to the $5.54 market price.
audit_findings.action: Deduct the filed $20.9 million cash payment or replace June 30 cash with a documented cash roll-forward through September 6, 2026; separately reconcile the $3.4 million dividend-equivalent settlement to the share denominator.

audit_findings.title: Recurring software reinvestment may be missing from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; 2025 purchases of property and equipment including capitalized software were $24.417 million, software amortization was $19.6 million, and gross cloud-implementation costs increased $0.9 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Any recurring capitalized software or cloud spending omitted from maintenance capex would overstate annual OE and its log-trend anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: We capitalize certain software development costs in the application development stage and upon the establishment of technological feasibility for a product.
audit_findings.explanation: Capitalization and recurring software investment are demonstrated, but the supplied record does not show the OE workpaper or establish that any expenditure was actually omitted. The potentially relevant filed spending is large compared with the $32.5 million anchor, but the filing combines software, equipment, tooling, and growth investment, so the recurring omitted amount and its materiality cannot be established.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each 2021-2025 OE calculation to cash purchases of property and equipment, capitalized software-development additions, and cloud-implementation additions; classify maintenance versus growth spending and rerun the anchor and scenarios for any demonstrated omission.

audit_findings.title: A static share ceiling may omit future dividend-equivalent dilution
audit_findings.magnitude: 757,259 dividend-equivalent RSUs and PRSUs granted in the first half of 2026; the May 2026 dividend provided another filed $3.4 million of dividend equivalents, but the resulting units are unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Additional dividend-equivalent units increase the future common-equity denominator and reduce value per share.
audit_findings.evidence: Outstanding restricted stock units and performance units are entitled to dividend equivalents in the form of additional unvested restricted stock units or unvested performance units equal in value to the amount of any declared dividend based on the closing price of the Company’s class A stock on the dividend payment date.
audit_findings.explanation: The dilution mechanism is demonstrated, but continuing dividend declarations, award vesting, forfeitures, and payment-date stock prices are forward-looking. The 243.58783 million ceiling appears broadly aligned with June 30 basic shares plus disclosed RSUs, maximum PRSUs, and options, but the record does not establish whether it includes the July 2026 units or future equivalents. Materiality cannot presently be measured, and maximum PRSU inclusion already makes the denominator conservative in another respect.
audit_findings.action: Add the actual units issued on July 21, 2026, confirm the ceiling's award-date cutoff, and update the denominator after every dividend using actual payment-date prices, vesting, forfeitures, and new grants.

audit_findings.title: The 2025 trend input contains a bad-debt reserve reversal
audit_findings.magnitude: $4.7 million pretax; conservatively treating the full amount as an OE reduction lowers the computed log-trend anchor from $32.5 million to approximately $31.1 million and value by about $0.07-$0.10 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: If unnormalized, the reversal raises 2025 OE and therefore the five-year log-trend anchor used in every scenario.
audit_findings.evidence: The decrease was primarily due to a $4.7 million net reversal of bad debt.
audit_findings.explanation: The $4.7 million reversal is demonstrated, but its inclusion in the $65.7 million OE input is unresolved. Even the conservative upper-bound test of subtracting the full pretax amount from OE reduces the anchor by only about $1.4 million, or 4.4%, and produces approximate scenario values of $2.69, $2.97, and $3.29 per share. These remain well below the $5.54 market price, so this finding cannot change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Confirm whether the 2025 OE workpaper already removes the reversal. If not, remove its after-tax amount and retain the rerun as a normalization sensitivity.

audit_findings.title: Product-margin improvement may include nonrepeatable inventory-reserve effects
audit_findings.magnitude: $19.706 million pretax net inventory-obsolescence benefit; approximately $14.0 million after tax using the filed 28.9% effective tax rate
audit_findings.mechanism: A nonrecurring reserve benefit can inflate 2025 OE and, through the log-trend calculation, raise the normalized anchor and every scenario's operating value.
audit_findings.evidence: The increase was primarily driven by a reduction in net inventory impairment charges and lower inventory procurement costs.
audit_findings.explanation: The reserve effect is demonstrated: the 2025 cash-flow statement reports a $19.706 million negative provision for inventory obsolescence, consistent with reserves declining from $49.015 million to $29.309 million. Whether the OE series already neutralizes it is unresolved. If the computed $14.0 million after-tax benefit remains in 2025 OE, removing it lowers the log-trend anchor to approximately $28.2 million and produces approximate values of $2.55, $2.80, and $3.09 per share, reductions of about $0.21-$0.30 per share. That is material to the stated valuation range even though it would reinforce, rather than reverse, the conclusion that market price exceeds intrinsic value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $19.706 million reserve benefit to 2025 cost of revenue and the OE workpaper, separate it from physical procurement savings, remove any unnormalized after-tax benefit, and rerun the trend anchor, all scenarios, and the buy-below price.
